subject: Dedicated Capacity Recap — NovaHealth (post-call)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novahealth.com>, Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated Capacity Recap — NovaHealth (post-call)

Hi Samantha / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Feel free to correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Occasional latency spikes during peak batch ingestion (affects clinical ingestion pipelines).
- Need for tenant isolation and strict data separation (HIPAA scope).
- Predictable unit-costs and capacity during product launches (planning for 3–6 month bursts).

Goals we discussed:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with network isolation (VPC) and customer-managed KMS.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability and P95 inference latency target under 250ms for single-turn prompts.
- Autoscale policy: baseline of 4 GPUs with ability to burst +2 nodes for short windows.
- Initial term: 6–12 month committed capacity to start, with option to expand.

Recommended starting configuration (what we committed to send):
- 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) in a dedicated pool
- VPC peering and private endpoints; HIPAA BA in place
- KV/prefix caching enabled for chat workloads; batching profile tuned for average seq len 512
- Monitoring: token-level cost and latency dashboards, per-route traces

Attachments: I attached the initial proposal and a capacity plan spreadsheet for your internal review.

Next steps:
1) I will send a formal proposal + SOW draft (attached) — target to have this to you by EOD Monday.
2) Dev (cc'd) will follow up on KMS/encryption and provide a short note on autoscale behavior under cold-start.
3) Samantha/Procurement to confirm procurement window and any required paperwork — Rajesh, any dates for procurement review?
4) Schedule a technical walkthrough with your infra team (30–45m) next week — propose Tue/Wed.

If that all looks right, we can turn the proposal into a DocuSign and start procurement. Thanks again — excited to partner.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@novahealth.com>

Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity Recap — NovaHealth (post-call)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- Budget/timing: We are in the middle of Q2 procurement reviews; decision window likely 4–6 weeks. We can commit to a pilot within that window.
- Compliance: HIPAA BA is required; also need SOC 2 Type II evidence. Can you confirm SOC 2 report availability and how audit logs are retained?
- Encryption: We prefer customer-managed keys (KMS) for at-rest encryption. Is HSM/KMS integration supported in the dedicated offering?

Also attaching a one-page network diagram for our infra team (see attachment).

Would like Dev to confirm the idle-to-burst behavior and the time to scale when a spike occurs. If we can get a short tech note on that, it will help procurement sign-off.

- Rajesh
Director of Infrastructure | NovaHealth
rajesh.iyer@novahealth.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 06:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity Recap — NovaHealth (post-call)

Thanks for the follow-up, Rajesh — happy to clarify. Short answers here, let me know if you want a longer tech write-up.

- SOC 2 / Audit logs: We can provide a current SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; audit logs (request/response metadata, timestamps, model version) are retained per contract (default 90 days, can extend). We can include log export to your SIEM via secure transfer.
- KMS/HSM: Yes — Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, Google KMS). We also offer HSM-backed keys for on-prem/private deployments. All data at rest is encrypted with the customer key; access is audited.
- Autoscale & cold-start: For a reserved pool of 4 GPUs with +2 burst nodes configured:
  - Baseline (4 GPUs) is warm; model instances and KV caches are kept resident.
  - Burst nodes provision in ~90–180s depending on region and image pull; warming to full steady-state may take additional 30–60s for large models as KV caches populate.
  - For spiky workloads we recommend pre-warming (scheduled or rule-triggered) around expected windows; we can also configure a small buffer of standby nodes to reduce scale latency (adds small incremental cost).

Attached is a draft SOW with the technical appendix and proposed autoscale policy. Let me know if you want us to tune the cache TTLs or batching profile before we finalize.

- Dev
